column2: then posted-interrupt delivery will be done by

column1: calling sync_pir_to_irr() at vmentry after interrupts are disabled.
sync_pir_to_irr() will check vmx->pi_desc.control ON bit and if

column2: it will sync vmx->pi_desc.pir to IRR and afterwards update RVI to

column1: ensure virtual-interrupt-delivery will dispatch interrupt to guest.
However
column2: it is possible that L1 will receive a posted-interrupt while

column1: CPU runs at host and is about to enter L2. In this case
sync_pir_to_irr() will indeed update the L1's APIC IRR but
vcpu_enter_guest() will then just resume into L2 guest without
re-evaluating if it should exit from L2 to L1 as a result of this
new pending L1 event.
To address this case
column2: if sync_pir_to_irr() has a new L1 injectable

column1: interrupt and CPU is running L2
column2: we force exit GUEST_MODE which will

column1: result in another iteration of vcpu_run() run loop which will call
kvm_vcpu_running() which will call check_nested_events() which will
handle the pending L1 event properly.
